title: Slow stock information
scenario: You maintain an online shop that sells a desk lamp. A customer clicks “Check availability” before deciding to buy, but the stock check keeps them waiting. The lamp description and price are already visible; the shop is waiting for a separate Inventory service to confirm stock.
why: A slow dependency can make a working shop feel unresponsive. You need to decide how long the customer should wait and what the shop can honestly show when it cannot confirm stock.
reproduce: Make Inventory replies 1500 ms (1.5 seconds) slower in Network Faults. Then click “Check availability” in Storefront. You are reproducing a slow stock check, not a complete outage.
ready: The stack starts healthy. Before this experiment, use “Clear all faults” in Network Faults and “Restore default settings” in the Fallbacks & timeouts tab if you changed mitigation settings earlier. Confirm that “Check availability” shows live stock. Opening this challenge does not apply a fault.
assignment: Can the shop respond sooner during a slow stock check without pretending the lamp is in stock?

tasks.title: Try the healthy customer journey
tasks.instruction: Open Storefront and click “Check availability” a few times. Record the displayed milliseconds and stock result. In Grafana, find /api/product under “Customer-facing p95 latency”. Write what you expect a 1.5-second Inventory delay to do and when you would stop the test.

tasks.title: Reproduce the customer complaint
tasks.instruction: Open Network Faults, choose Inventory, set “Response delay (ms)” to 1500, and click “Apply delay”. Return to Storefront and click “Check availability” again. Look for the longer wait; with default settings, the request should normally still succeed.

tasks.title: Find evidence of the cause
tasks.instruction: Record the new request times and compare them with your healthy measurements. In Grafana, compare /api/product in “Customer-facing p95 latency” with inventory in “Dependency p95 latency”. Use a fresh 60–90-second window per phase so old data does not dominate the comparison.

tasks.title: Change how the shop handles the delay
tasks.instruction: Remove the Inventory delay first. In Network Faults, open “Fallbacks & timeouts” and click “Use Challenge 1 settings”. This enables Inventory fallback with a 400 ms timeout immediately. The timeout limits the wait; the fallback lets the shop return “Stock unconfirmed”. No source-code edit is required.

tasks.title: Repeat, compare, and clean up
tasks.instruction: Apply the same 1500 ms Inventory delay again. Repeat “Check availability” and record the response time, displayed stock message, and “Fallback activity” in Grafana. Explain the speed-versus-certainty trade-off. Clear faults, click “Restore default settings” in Fallbacks & timeouts, check live stock returns, then submit your notes below.

done: You recorded the same customer action in three states: healthy, delayed, and delayed with mitigation.
You explained whether the response became faster and why “Stock unconfirmed” is different from confirmed availability.
You removed the fault, restored the defaults, and submitted your own measurements.
solution: Healthy: product requests succeed with low local latency. Record your own baseline; exact numbers vary.
With +1500 ms Inventory latency and the default 3000 ms timeout, product latency should rise by roughly 1500 ms. Inventory call latency rises too; requests normally still succeed.

Example mitigation: in Fallbacks & timeouts, apply a 400 ms Inventory timeout with Inventory fallback enabled. Under the same fault, the page should return sooner with stock marked unconfirmed. Fallback counts rise.
Trade-off: a fast HTTP 200 is not confirmed stock. Clear the fault, click “Restore default settings”, and check that normal stock returns.

fields.label: Healthy baseline and metric
fields.prompt: Which route and metric did you choose? Include your measured baseline.

fields.label: Hypothesis and abort condition
fields.prompt: What did you expect from +1500 ms Inventory latency, and when would you stop?

fields.label: Fault evidence
fields.prompt: Record the same route under fault: latency, success rate, Inventory signal, and time window.

fields.label: Mitigation and reason
fields.prompt: What timeout/fallback did you use, and why is it safe for a product page?

fields.label: Same-fault validation
fields.prompt: What happened when you applied the identical fault after mitigation?

fields.label: Conclusion and cleanup
fields.prompt: Did resilience improve? What information is now uncertain? Confirm that the fault was removed.

overview.title: 1 · Slow stock check
overview.description: Add a 1.5-second Inventory delay. Can the shop respond sooner while saying stock is unconfirmed?

mitigationHelp.description: The fallback is already implemented. Enable it with these settings: wait at most 400 ms for Inventory, then return “Stock unconfirmed” if it cannot answer. The delay itself remains a separate setting in Network Faults.
mitigationHelp.instruction: In Network Faults, open “Fallbacks & timeouts” and click “Use Challenge 1 settings”. Or set Inventory timeout to 400, check “Enable Inventory fallback”, and click “Apply Inventory settings”.
